findings.title: Retry cleanup is not restricted to SMS reminders
findings.body: The `retryCount > 1` branch is a separate `OR` condition, so it deletes any `WorkflowReminder` with two retries, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders, regardless of its scheduled date or status. This SMS cron should scope the retry predicate to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` as well; otherwise a populated retry count on another workflow method causes that reminder to be silently deleted.

findings.title: Retry count updates can lose concurrent failures
findings.body: The retry value is computed from the value read by `findMany` and written back as `reminder.retryCount + 1` (with the same pattern in the catch block). Overlapping cron invocations can both read `0`, both fail scheduling, and both write `1`, even though there were two failures. The reminder then remains eligible for an additional attempt instead of being removed at the configured limit. Use an atomic Prisma increment, and condition the update on the reminder still being unscheduled so a concurrent successful scheduler cannot be counted as a failure.

findings.title: Reminders without a recipient or message never consume retries
findings.body: Both new retry updates are inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)`. `WorkflowStep.sendTo` and `Booking.smsReminderNumber` are optional, so an SMS reminder with no configured phone number reaches this guard, remains `scheduled: false` with `retryCount: 0`, and is selected again on every cron run until its scheduled date. This leaves the missing/invalid-recipient case the PR is intended to stop retrying; treat a missing destination or unrenderable message as a terminal failure or increment the retry count outside this guard.
